title: Adrian Peterson's 2004 Freshman Season: 1,925 Yards at OU
question: How many yards did Adrian Peterson rush for as a freshman at Oklahoma?
answer: Adrian Peterson ran for 1,925 yards on a nation-leading 339 carries as a true freshman in 2004, an NCAA freshman record, and finished second in the Heisman voting.
summary: Adrian Peterson ran for an NCAA freshman record 1,925 yards in 2004 and became the first freshman to finish as Heisman runner-up, behind USC's Matt Leinart.
body: Sooner fans knew Adrian Peterson was special the moment he arrived from Palestine, Texas. Few expected him to rewrite the freshman record book in a single autumn.

Peterson opened his career with nine straight 100-yard games and reached 1,000 rushing yards in just his seventh college game, faster than any freshman had before. By the end of the 2004 season he had carried 339 times, the most in the nation, for 1,925 yards, the most ever by a first-year college player at that point. His 11 games of 100 yards or more also set an NCAA freshman mark.

Some of his biggest days came on the biggest stages. He rushed for 183 yards and two touchdowns against Oregon and piled up 225 yards in a 12-0 win over Texas. Oklahoma went 12-0 before the postseason and earned a spot in the national championship game, where USC beat the Sooners in the Orange Bowl.

The honors followed. Peterson was a unanimous All-American, the Big 12 Offensive Freshman of the Year and a Doak Walker Award finalist. In the Heisman vote he finished second to USC quarterback Matt Leinart, becoming the first freshman ever to finish as runner-up, with teammate Jason White third.

That season was a preview. The Minnesota Vikings drafted Peterson seventh overall in 2007, and in 2012 he was named NFL MVP after rushing for 2,097 yards, nine short of Eric Dickerson's single-season record.
